stories.title: Trump: no strike on Iran before the midterms
stories.body: President Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections, describing talks as productive. Vice-President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful cut to its uranium enrichment capacity, which experts see as softer than the earlier demand to end enrichment completely. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would answer the US response to its seven-day Hormuz plan within days. Iranian media reported explosions in the southern Strait, possibly from sea mines.
stories.why: Oil prices swing on every signal from Washington and Tehran, which feeds straight into Nigeria's fuel and budget planning.

cards.front: What did US Vice-President Vance demand of Iran in October 2026?
cards.back: A meaningful cut to its uranium enrichment capacity (Iran has reached 60% enrichment).

stories.title: Lakurawa attack halts work on Sokoto–Badagry highway
stories.body: Suspected Lakurawa fighters attacked a construction site of the Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway at Gubba village, Maiyama LGA, Kebbi State. Two security personnel and a foreign worker were killed and two civilians wounded. Police said the attackers came from the Kebbe area of Sokoto State, and construction has been suspended.
stories.why: Attacks on major federal road projects show how insecurity in the North-west slows Nigeria's economic plans.

stories.title: ISWAP commander killed in Ondo with UK help
stories.body: The State Security Service (SSS) said an intelligence-led operation with the Army and Amotekun killed Abdussamad Ohida, known as Anwar, a senior ISWAP commander, in Owo forest, Ondo State. The SSS said he was planning attacks in southern states during the festive season and the 2027 elections. It said intelligence partners from the UK helped, the first time the UK has been publicly named in such an operation.
stories.why: It shows jihadist groups reaching into the South-west and the growing role of foreign intelligence partnerships.

cards.front: Which ISWAP commander was killed in Owo forest in October 2026?
cards.back: Abdussamad Ohida ("Anwar"), in an SSS-led operation aided by UK intelligence.

stories.title: Sudan's army pushes the RSF back in Kordofan
stories.body: Sudan's army said it captured al-Mazroub in North Kordofan, a town linking army-held areas to the RSF stronghold of West Kordofan. The army also claimed gains in Blue Nile state. The RSF still holds almost all of Darfur after taking El Fasher in October 2025, so the main front has moved to Kordofan. The war has displaced 14 million people.
stories.why: Sudan is Africa's largest humanitarian crisis, and its arms and fighters flow across the Sahel.

stories.title: Ukraine ready for three-way talks by end of October
stories.body: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for US-backed talks with Russia before the end of October, possibly in the United Arab Emirates. He spoke during a visit to Kyiv by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Moscow has also said it is open to October talks. Both sides are stepping up strikes on energy and transport as winter approaches.
stories.why: Any deal or escalation moves world wheat, fertiliser and fuel prices, which feed Nigerian inflation.

cards.front: Where are US–Ukraine–Russia talks proposed for October 2026?
cards.back: The United Arab Emirates (or another US-proposed venue).

stories.title: Gaza ceasefire keeps fraying
stories.body: An Israeli strike on an apartment in Gaza City killed at least five people, and eight Palestinians were killed across Gaza that day. Israel said it was targeting Ali al-Amoudi, a senior Hamas official. At least 1,400 people have been killed in Gaza since the ceasefire began in October 2025. Gaza health authorities put the total war death toll since 7 October 2023 at more than 74,000.
stories.why: Nigeria backs a two-state solution, and the Gaza file is a standard current-affairs interview question.

cards.front: Roughly how many people had been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, by October 2026?
